Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules (uredinia) that break through the leaf surface, appearing on both upper and lower sides of the leaves.
treatment: Apply foliar fungicides containing strobilurins or triazoles if rust pustules appear early in the season and threaten the upper canopy
No direct treatment needed if infection occurs close to crop maturity
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids and manage residue by tilling or rotating crops to disrupt local spore accumulation.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green or tan lesions that progress to resemble a cigar shape, typically appearing first on lower leaves.
treatment: Apply protective or curative foliar fungicides early from the whorl stage to silking if lesions appear before tasseling
Shred and bury crop residue post-harvest to speed up microbial breakdown of fungal structures
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Utilize highly resistant hybrid choices and stick to a minimum 1-year crop rotation out of corn.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Distinctly rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions restricted by parallel leaf veins, initially presenting as small spots with yellow halos.
treatment: Apply active triazole or strobilurin-based fungicides if weather forecasts project continuous high humidity and lesions reach the ear leaf
Incorporate deep fall tillage to submerge and destroy overwintering fungus layers in the soil
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Practice a strict 2-year crop rotation sequence with non-host crops like soybeans or alfalfa to break the fungus life cycle.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are completely green, erect, and broad without any brown lesions, spotting, or rust pustules. Stalks are robust and firm.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Ensure optimal nitrogen fertilization, uniform plant population spacing, and standard seasonal weed suppression.
